column3: The Hebrew repeats the king’s name in identifying him; BSB expresses the identification as a relative clause.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names the force of Persia and Media; BSB specifies military leaders.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew orders the ranks from great to small; BSB reverses them.
The Hebrew lists the couches without a verb of arranging them; BSB supplies that they were arranged.
The Hebrew describes the quantity of royal wine according to the king’s hand; BSB describes its free flow according to his bounty.
The Hebrew says there was no compulsion in drinking; BSB says there was no limit.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew speaks of peoples in the plural; BSB says the people.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the king spoke to the wise men; BSB describes consultation.
The Hebrew describes men seeing the king’s face and sitting first in the kingdom; BSB interprets this as personal access and highest rank.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes husbands as despised in the women’s eyes; BSB omits the image of eyes.
The Hebrew leaves the content of what the noble women will say unstated; BSB supplies the same thing.
The Hebrew says the king should give her royal position to another; BSB uses a passive clause.
The Hebrew places great to small after the husbands; BSB reverses the order and applies it to the women.
The Hebrew describes the matter as good in their eyes; BSB says they were pleased with the counsel.
The Hebrew also says each man should speak the language of his people; BSB omits this final phrase.
